message.content:
You are reverse-engineering a PyInstaller-frozen Python program to port it to Node.js.

The executable is at /workspace/dataset/test8_executable. Run it with Bash. NEVER use the `python` command; only run the executable.
The Python source it was built from is:

```python
import argparse
from bidict import bidict

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('--k1', type=str, required=True)
parser.add_argument('--v1', type=int, required=True)
parser.add_argument('--k2', type=str, required=True)
parser.add_argument('--v2', type=int, required=True)
parser.add_argument('--k3', type=str, required=True)
parser.add_argument('--v3', type=int, required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()

b = bidict()
b[args.k1] = args.v1
b[args.k2] = args.v2
b[args.k3] = args.v3
print(b)
print(b[args.k1])
print(b.inv[args.v2])
print(b.inv[args.v3])
b[args.k1] = 999
print(b)
```

IMPORTANT method notes:
- Capture stdout and stderr SEPARATELY so you know which stream each line goes to. Example:
  `/workspace/dataset/test8_executable --k1 a --v1 1 --k2 b --v2 2 --k3 c --v3 3 >/tmp/o.txt 2>/tmp/e.txt; echo "RC=$?"; echo "--STDOUT--"; cat -A /tmp/o.txt; echo "--STDERR--"; cat -A /tmp/e.txt`
  (use `cat -A` or `od -c` when whitespace/newlines/escapes matter, so you see exact bytes)
- Use single-quoted shell args to pass literal quotes/backslashes safely, or use printf/env tricks for exotic bytes.
- Already-established baseline facts (do not re-derive, build on them):
  * Normal run prints 5 lines: repr(b), b[k1], b.inv[v2], b.inv[v3], repr(b-after-update).
  * repr format: `bidict({'i': 55, 'c': 95, 't': 92})`
  * Setting a NEW key to an ALREADY-PRESENT value -> stderr traceback ending `bidict.ValueDuplicationError: <value>`, rc=1.
  * Setting an EXISTING key to a value already held by a DIFFERENT key -> `bidict.KeyAndValueDuplicationError: ('<key>', <value>)`, rc=1.
  * Setting an existing key to the value it ALREADY has -> no error, no-op.
  * Re-assigning an existing key a fresh value keeps that key's ORIGINAL insertion position.
  * Missing required args -> usage + `test8_executable: error: the following arguments are required: --v1, --k2, ...` on stderr, rc=2.
  * Bad int -> `test8_executable: error: argument --v1: invalid int value: 'x'`, rc=2.
  * Negative values like `--v1 -5` parse fine.

Report EXACT bytes. Your final output is consumed by a porter who cannot run the executable, so be exhaustive and literal. Quote exact strings.

---

Close this specific gap in the port spec by RUNNING the executable. Report byte-exact observations.

Gap: Short-option clustering rule for `-h` is stated wrong. The real rule: any single-dash token whose FIRST character after '-' is 'h' fires help and ignores the rest — `-hh`, `-hx`, `-h5` all print help, rc=0. But `-xh` does NOT (unknown token `-xh`, reported verbatim as one extra / triggers the required error). And `-h=x` / `-h=` / `--help=` / `--hel=x` all give `argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument 'x'` / `... ''` — note the EMPTY explicit arg form `''` was never captured by any probe.
Why it matters: The spec explains `-hh` as '-h then -h', which wrongly predicts `-xh` -> help and gives no rule for `-hx`/`-h5`. The `''` payload for `-h=` / `--help=` is a distinct message a port must emit.
Suggested command: cd /workspace/dataset && for a in "-hh" "-hx" "-h5" "-xh" "-h=x" "-h=" "--help=" "--hel=x"; do echo "=== $a"; ./test8_executable $a >/tmp/o.txt 2>/tmp/e.txt; echo RC=$?; head -1 /tmp/o.txt|cat -A; tail -1 /tmp/e.txt|cat -A; done

Go beyond the suggested command if needed to fully pin the rule.

input.implementationNotes:
Implement argparse's exact single-dash cluster algorithm. Only two option strings are registered: '-h' and '--help' (plus the long value-taking '--k1/--v1/--k2/--v2/--k3/--v3'). Prefix char set is {'-'}. TOKEN CLASSIFICATION (left-to-right over argv; a standalone '--' switches everything after it to positional): 1. Empty token '' or token not starting with '-' -> positional. 2. Token exactly '-' (length 1) -> positional. 3. Token exactly '-h' or '--help' -> HELP, no explicit arg. 4. Token starts with '--': split at FIRST '=' into (left, payload) — payload is null if no '='. If left is a non-empty prefix of '--help' (i.e. '--h', '--he', '--hel', '--help'; abbreviation is enabled) -> HELP action with that payload. (Other '--' prefixes match the k/v options or are ambiguous/unknown — out of scope here.) 5. Token starts with '-' and token[1] != '-': let head = token[0:2], tail = token[2:]. - If head != '-h' -> UNKNOWN OPTION: the ENTIRE token verbatim goes to the extras list (never help, never split). - If head == '-h' -> HELP action with (sep, explicit) computed as: if tail starts with '=' then sep='=', explicit=tail[1:]; else sep='', explicit=tail (explicit is null when tail is empty). HELP-ACTION CONSUMPTION LOOP (for a single-dash '-h...' token; '-h' takes 0 arguments): queuedHelp = false loop: if explicit is null -> queuedHelp = true; FIRE if explicit == '' -> ERROR ignoredExplicit('') // e.g. '-h=' if sep == '=' -> ERROR ignoredExplicit(explicit) // e.g. '-h=x', '-hh=x' if explicit[0] == '-' -> ERROR ignoredExplicit(explicit) // e.g. '-h-', '-h-x', '-h--k1', '-hh--' // otherwise peel one char and continue queuedHelp = true next = '-' + explicit[0]; rest = explicit[1:] if next == '-h': if rest == '' -> FIRE if rest[0] == '=' -> sep='='; explicit=rest[1:]; continue else -> sep=''; explicit=rest; continue else: extras.push('-' + explicit) // whole remaining cluster, unreported because help fires FIRE FIRE = print the 193-byte help text to stdout and exit(0) immediately. For the LONG form (case 4) there is no peeling: if payload is null -> FIRE; else -> ERROR ignoredExplicit(payload) (payload may be ''). NET OBSERVABLE RULE for single-dash tokens: with R = token[2:] after a leading '-h', R == '' -> help, rc 0 R starts with '=' -> ERROR ignoredExplicit(R[1:]) (empty -> '') R[0] == '-' -> ERROR ignoredExplicit(R) R[0] not in {'-','=','h'} -> help, rc 0 (rest silently discarded) R[0] == 'h' -> recurse with token = '-' + R Help is printed at most ONCE no matter how many 'h's. ERROR OUTPUT SHAPE (all rc=2, stdout EMPTY, both lines on stderr, each newline-terminated): line 1: "usage: test8_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2 --k3 K3 --v3 V3" line 2: "test8_executable: error: " + msg ignoredExplicit(p) msg = "argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '

'" — the action label is ALWAYS the joined "-h/--help" regardless of the spelling typed, and

is Python repr-style single-quoted, so an empty payload renders as two adjacent quotes: '' (this empty form is produced by '-h=', '--help=', '--h='). PRECEDENCE (strict left-to-right consumption): - An error raised while consuming an EARLIER token beats a later help token ('--v1 x -h' -> invalid int error; '--k1 -h' / '--k1 -hx' -> "argument --k1: expected one argument"). - A help token beats everything to its RIGHT and beats the required-arguments check, the unrecognized-extras check, and the program body: rc=0, only help on stdout. - 'ignored explicit argument' errors are raised during consumption, so they beat the required-args and extras checks too. - Unrecognized extras are only reported AFTER a successful parse: required-args error (rc=2) takes precedence when any of --k1..--v3 is missing; otherwise "unrecognized arguments: " + extras joined by a single space, in argv order, verbatim (rc=2, program body never runs, stdout empty). HELP TEXT (exactly 193 bytes, stdout, single trailing newline): "usage: test8_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2 --k3 K3 --v3 V3\n\noptions:\n -h, --help show this help message and exit\n --k1 K1\n --v1 V1\n --k2 K2\n --v2 V2\n --k3 K3\n --v3 V3\n" (two-space indent on option lines; '-h, --help' followed by two spaces before 'show'; the k/v lines have no help text.)
